policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 31:12 spells the name "Conaniah", whose first syllable carries an o-vowel. That o is supplied by the waw of the ketiv כונניהו (Konanyahu); the qere כָּֽנַנְיָ֣הוּ is pointed with patach and would be rendered "Cananiah". The ASV's own wording therefore distinguishes the ketiv here.

ASV 31:13 again spells the name "Conaniah" with an o-vowel in the first syllable, matching the waw of the ketiv כונניהו rather than the patach of the qere כָּֽנַנְיָ֨הוּ֙, which would give "Cananiah". Decided from this verse's English alone, on the same ground as the reading it names in 31:12.
